answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity proof of sequential work: each agent attaches a verifiable delay function output, a puzzle needing fixed wall-clock time to solve but milliseconds to check. One machine certifies only a few keys per hour, however free accounts are to create. To push a ripple of fake votes through the wharf, an attacker must fund a vine of compute for each extra key; a thousand Sybils need a thousand times the sequential work, and parallel hardware costs real money. Cheap verification keeps the network light while the delay makes every forged identity pay for itself.
